Who we are

Smita Prasad · Founder & Creative Director

⚜ Boutique Agency · Classical CommunityMusic · Dance · Art · HeritageShowcases & Exhibitions
EngineerPainterBharatanatyam Artist

Smita Prasad is an engineer, a painter and a Bharatanatyam artist. Alapadma brings these worlds together, blending discipline, creativity and classical tradition to create events with heart.

Alapadma, named after the blooming-lotus hand gesture (alapadma mudra) of Indian classical dance, is a boutique agency and classical community that brings communities, creators and corporates together through music, dance, art and heritage, with showcases and exhibitions at its heart.

Why this matters now

Heritage and tribal-livelihood platforms are drawing national attention

1,000+

Tribal artisans, chefs and troupes took part in Bharat Tribes Fest 2026 in New Delhi, which was extended to 5 April due to public response.

600+

Tribal entrepreneurs gathered at Aadi Mahotsav 2025, a nine-day national showcase of tribal craft, cuisine and commerce.

Gap

Artisans still need direct market access, fair price realisation and digital visibility. That is the space Alapadma activates for brands.

Supporting Tribal & Folk Dances

Giving traditional performers a stage, an audience and a livelihood

Alapadma works with tribal and folk dance communities whose costumes, music and movement carry centuries of living heritage. Our events bring these performers to new audiences, honour their craft and help sustain the traditions.

Sponsors can power performances, documentation and artisan showcases, and be part of keeping these art forms alive.

Supporting Art & Artists

Classical dance, painting and craft, all part of one living heritage

Alapadma celebrates every form of Indian art, from dance and music to painting and handcrafted work. We create spaces where artists can show their work, tell their stories and reach people who value them.

Sponsors help us exhibit, document and sell the work of emerging artists, so creative talent can build a livelihood.

Creating Work in the Arts

Alapadma is also a source of livelihood for creative people

Our Own Dance Production

We are developing an original Alapadma dance production, built around classical and folk traditions. A sponsor-ready property in the making.

Employing Creative Talent

Every Alapadma event gives paid work to musicians, dancers, choreographers, technicians and event crews.

Opportunities in Media

Photographers, filmmakers, editors and content creators are engaged to document and share our programmes with wider audiences.

When you sponsor Alapadma, your support goes beyond one evening. It creates real work for artists and professionals across music, dance and media.

Creating Value for the Nation

We hire people. We pay artists. We turn culture into livelihood.

Artists Are Paid

Every performer, musician and craftsperson on an Alapadma stage is paid for their work, because heritage survives when its keepers can earn from it.

People Get Hired

We employ and engage dancers, musicians, technicians, media professionals and event teams, creating steady work in the creative economy.

Culture Becomes Economy

Every ticket sold and every sponsor on board circulates money to artists and communities, strengthening India's cultural economy.

Partner With Purpose

Five purpose-led platforms, each built for measurable brand impact

Diversity & Inclusion Employee Engagement

Immersive workshops, craft circles and performances for your teams, aligned to DEI and culture calendars. Co-branded sessions in office or on site.

Digital Preservation of Cultural Heritage

Documenting folk arts, rituals and craft techniques as films, photo archives and reels, with sponsor credit on every asset.

Economic Empowerment of Tribal Artisans

Pop-up marketplaces, direct-to-buyer showcases and CSR-linked procurement that put income in artisans' hands.

Connecting Bharat

Cross-region cultural exchanges linking urban audiences with rural and tribal creators, online and on the ground.

Celebrating Rural Resilience

Stories and live celebrations of farmers, weavers and village communities that carry traditions forward.

Sponsor fit: Our upcoming Odissi Masterclass suits Digital Preservation of Cultural Heritage, Diversity & Inclusion Employee Engagement and Connecting Bharat.
